label: Ideal consensus and due actuality comparison
definition: Consensus means approval by every assessor in a supplied class. Reduction identifies aspect goodness with that consensus. Acceptance requires every due actuality to receive all approvals. SoundWitness requires for each aspect some assessor whose approval implies due actuality; it need not be the same assessor for every aspect. These are open analyst bridges, not a historical attribution or practical obligation.
note: Issue #1116. Empty classes make consensus vacuous; Controls tests that case and omission of each bridge. No claim that real ideal assessors exist or that an idealization is normatively authoritative. See docs/notes/goodness-form-end-definitions.md.
